items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: So after the show, and things, he called me over. This is Irving Mills, yeah. "Want you to go with Ellington."

ctx.x: Well, "No, we got contracts," and so and so. So Les Hite Height, who at that time was leader of the band, and we got together and talked, and he said, "Oh, well, if he wants to go, let's let him go. We'll let him see the East," and like that. So I quit on a Tuesday, was my last day. After that Tuesday this Irving Mills came in the place, and there again we were doing, as I was doing, a lot of soloing. I had a solo in the show, the floor show. I was playing "Trees." You know, the old religious piece, "Trees." And…
And so this Irving Mills was in the audience. So after the show, and things, he called me over. This is Irving Mills, yeah. "Want you to go with Ellington." Well, the

gist of it was, I quit on a Tuesday, and on a Saturday I was on the train, heading East with Ellington's outfit. I'd never -- I'd seen Ellington the couple of times he was out there, but I wasn't particularly -- you know, it's all right.
